pages.text: A photon absorbed breaks one bond, and the chain of reactions it starts makes Φ molecules of product (the quantum yield). The mixture absorbs a fraction 1 − 10^(−A) of the light, where A = εcl (Beer-Lambert): ε how strongly the molecule absorbs, c its concentration, l the path through the cell.
$(thing)Set$(): Lamp intensity, Path length.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Lamp ageing: the intensity varies by ±3%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The lamp is cooking the cell.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More light absorbed, more product.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Absorbance: A = εcl$(br)Fraction absorbed: f = 1 − 10^(−A)$(br)Reaction rate: r = Φ·I·f
